name: Hinduri
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India. 2023. Linguistic Survey of India: Himachal Pradesh. New Delhi.
sources.note: No Hinduri/Handuri chapter at all (contents: Bharmauri, Churahi, Chambeali, Kangri, Keonthali, Kulvi, Mandeali, Pangwali, Sanori, Sirmauri, Bhateali, Bilaspuri, Dogri, Nepali, Kinnauri, Lahauli, Bhotia); Hinduri only named as the Pahari 'in Nalagarh' and in mother-tongue tables (Handuri 47,803 in 2011).

sources.citation: Dutt, Ishwari. 1978. Baghati boli ka bhashavaigyanik adhyayan [A linguistic study of the Baghati dialect]. PhD thesis, Dept. of Hindi, Panjab University, Chandigarh (guide D. D. Sharma). xxi+286 pp. Shodhganga hdl 10603/111863. Ch. 1 sec. 1.5-1.6, pp. 51-53.
sources.note: NEIGHBOURING DIALECT (Baghati of Solan/Kasauli = Mahasu Pahari; the thesis map excludes Nalagarh/Ramshahr). Baghati has three phonemic tones, usually one tone-bearing syllable per word; p. 53: monosyllables carry tone; in disyllables the second syllable carries it if the first is short and the second long, otherwise the first; in longer words the first short or second long syllable; sec. 1.6 'svaraghat star' = three pitch levels + terminal contours (intonation), not word stress. Not a statement about Hinduri.

sources.citation: Sanyukta. 1966. Mixed dialects bordering on Panjabi, Pahari and Khari Boli. PhD thesis, Panjab University. ix+574 pp. Shodhganga hdl 10603/94076 (preface, contents, Introduction downloaded).
sources.note: Checked for coverage only: study area = Ambala, northern Karnal and former Sirmur state, bounded on the west by the Ghaggar, so Nalagarh/Handuri is outside it. Irrelevant to hind1267.

sources.citation: Angiras, Amar Dev. 2017. Himachali pariprekshya mem Solan janpad: itihas evam sanskriti [Solan district in Himachali perspective: history and culture]. Arki: Dayavanti Prakashan. (Hindi) pp. 234-238 'Solan janpad ki pramukh boliyam'.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Treats hill-Handuri, Kunihari and Mahlogi as sub-dialects of Baghli (Baghal/Arki), rejects Grierson's subordination of Handuri/Baghli to Baghati; only phonological remark is de-aspiration of voiced aspirates (jhagra > 'chagra', bhala > 'pala').

sources.citation: Indian Institute of Advanced Study. 2002. Pahari bhasha tatha sahitya (seminar papers, Hindi). Shimla: IIAS.
sources.note: Handuri only in a quoted LSI classification passage ('inke purvi bhagom ki boli Handuri pahari hai'); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Varma, Siddheshwar. 1978. Pahari Language: A Linguistic Analysis (G. A. Grierson's LSI, a summary). Panjab University Indological Series 19. Hoshiarpur: VVRI. 'Handuri' section in 'The Kiunthali group' (c. p. 72).
sources.note: Verbatim digest of LSI pp. 586-587; silent on stress/accent.

sources.citation: Bailey, T. Grahame. 1920 [preface 1915]. Linguistic Studies from the Himalayas (Asiatic Society Monographs). London: RAS. 'The Bilaspur and Nalagarh dialects: Introduction' pp. 231-232; 'Handuri' notes p. 235; 'Handuri (East Nalagarh)' paradigms pp. c. 260-264.
sources.note: Nothing for Handuri: declension/conjugation tables and a note that Handuri 'closely resembles Kiunthali'; the book's accent remarks (preface on tones; per-word 'accent on first/second' notes) belong to other dialects, none in the Handuri section.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1916. Linguistic Survey of India, vol. IX part IV: Pahari languages and Gujuri. Calcutta. 'Handuri' (Kiunthali group), pp. 586-592: introduction + skeleton grammar pp. 586-587, specimen pp. 588-592.
sources.note: Nothing. Handuri is called 'a transitional form of speech.. a mixture of Kiunthali and Panjabi'; only nouns, pronouns, verbs and one Parable specimen are given; no pronunciation or accent paragraph (the Kiunthali-group introduction pp. ~549 ff. also has no accent statement).

sources.citation: Punjab States Gazetteer vol. VIII: Gazetteer of the Simla Hill States, 1910. Lahore 1911. Nalagarh State chapter; appendix 'Dialects of the Simla Hills' by T. G. Bailey.
sources.note: Nothing; the Nalagarh chapter has no language section and Bailey's appendix states the dialects of 'Bilaspur, Nalagarh, Jubbal and Bashahr.. still require to be investigated'.
Bibliographic check only: references are LSI IX.iv pp. 586-592, Ethnologue, Census, UNESCO Atlas; no phonological source; Glottolog has no descriptive reference.

sources.citation: Devy, G. N. (gen. ed.). People's Linguistic Survey of India, vol. 11 part 2: The Languages of Himachal Pradesh. New Delhi: Orient BlackSwan (English ed., c. 2015-2017; volume editors not verified here). Any Handuri/Hinduri or Baghliani entry.
